policy_presence.summary: TUM provides AI guidance across ProLehre didactic guidelines, the APSO examination statute reading version, SGwP research integrity statute, and chair-level thesis guidelines.

coursework.summary: TUM ProLehre student guidance specifies that generative AI tools may be used for written coursework, term papers, essays, and theses only when AI tool use is explicitly permitted for that specific assessment by the instructor or module specifications. Where instructions are silent, students should ask in advance rather than assuming permission. When authorized, transparent documentation of tool use and prompts is commonly required, and students retain full personal responsibility for submitted work.

exams.summary: Examinations prohibit unauthorized generative AI assistance. Under the reviewed APSO reading version, suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under APSO § 24(6), an examination failed due to § 22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. Severe or repeated deception or disruption may lead to degree-program exclusion under § 22(3); these are general examination provisions rather than an AI-specific sanction schedule.

ai_disclosure.summary: When generative AI tool use is authorized, transparent documentation of tool use, methods, and prompts is commonly required and course-conditioned; students retain full personal responsibility for all submitted work. The Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research guidelines require a signed AI declaration for theses and seminar papers, including a formal non-use declaration if no AI was used.

privacy_data_entry.summary: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, which applies also to TUM-approved systems. In addition, teaching and study materials (such as lecture slides, scripts, recordings, or past exams) are protected intellectual property and require explicit instructor consent before being uploaded to or processed in AI tools, even when used solely for personal study purposes like summarization, transcription, or translation.

academic_integrity.summary: Under the reviewed APSO reading version, attempted deception in examinations or coursework results in an assessment grade of 5.0 (fail). A failed examination resulting from deception or disruption may be retaken only once under § 24(6). Under § 25(3), a candidate may inspect examination files upon reasoned written application to the examination board chair within 1 month of grade announcement, with time and place determined by the chair with the examiner. Under § 21, procedural defects must be raised promptly in writing. Formally published enactments remain legally authoritative over the reading consolidation. The inspection window is not a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.

approved_tools.summary: TUM provides M365 Copilot Chat through TUMonline activation, but tool activation does not establish assessment permission or authorization to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data. ProLehre highlights Chat-AI by AcademicCloud as a privacy-friendly option hosted on German university servers, but reviewed sources do not establish individual account eligibility or licensing guarantees.

named_ai_services.summary: TUM provides M365 Copilot Chat through TUMonline activation, but tool activation does not establish assessment permission or authorization to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data. ProLehre highlights Chat-AI by AcademicCloud as a privacy-friendly option hosted on German university servers, but reviewed sources do not establish individual account eligibility or licensing guarantees.

teaching_guidance.summary: TUM ProLehre provides didactic guidance for instructors on designing learning-outcomes-based AI policies, setting clear task boundaries, and training students in critical AI evaluation.

research_guidance.summary: TUM SGwP statutes establish research integrity standards requiring research data retention on durable secure media, ordinarily for 10 years from publication unless justified shorter periods or discipline-specific standards apply. Guidelines from the MKT Chair permit AI as a research aid for theses but prohibit AI empirical data collection and analysis unless explicitly approved by the supervisor.

security_procurement.summary: M365 Copilot Chat is released for TUM members after TUMonline activation. ProLehre prohibits entering personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, including university-approved systems.
